questions.question: Explain what the Underground Railroad was and how it worked, using its code words.
questions.expected_answer: A secret, loose network of routes, safe houses and people (mainly free Black communities, formerly enslaved people and white allies such as Quakers) that helped enslaved people escape to the free North and Canada from about the 1830s to 1860. Conductors guided escapers; stations were safe houses run by stationmasters; passengers were the escapers; stockholders gave money and supplies; terminals were final destinations.

questions.question: Describe the dangers faced by enslaved people who tried to escape and two methods they used.
questions.expected_answer: Dangers: long journeys on foot at night through forests, swamps and rivers; hunger and cold; slave catchers with dogs and reward hunters; patrols; punishment of whipping, branding, sale further south or death; after 1850, the Fugitive Slave Act made the North unsafe. Methods: following the North Star and rivers; disguises and forged passes; help from other enslaved people and the Underground Railroad; travelling in winter or at weekends.

questions.question: Summarise the contribution of Harriet Tubman to the struggle against slavery.
questions.expected_answer: Born enslaved in Maryland about 1822, she escaped in 1849 and returned about 13 times to lead about 70 people, including family members, to freedom and helped others with instructions, never losing anyone; she was called Moses. After 1850 she led people to Canada. In the Civil War she worked as a nurse and spy and helped lead the 1863 Combahee River Raid that freed over 700 people; she later cared for the poor and supported women's votes.
